name: Question 8
worked_solution:
First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+(kx)^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(kx)+C
$$

We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1/(2\sqrt{3})}\frac{6}{1+36{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =6\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{1/(2\sqrt{3})}\frac{1}{1+36{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =6\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{1/(2\sqrt{3})}\frac{1}{1+(6x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =6\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6x)]}_{a}^{1/(2\sqrt{3})} \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6a)] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6a)].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6x),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6x)]=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6x)]=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/faa31c8261818c5c978d984a9b90a13e58794b02ff6f47e868ad6d5a06b7f71a.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1/(2\sqrt{3})}\frac{6}{1+36{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{\pi }{3}-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(6a)] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}-(-\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

∫−∞1/(23)61+36x2dx=6⋅lima→−∞∫a1/(23)11+36x2dx=6⋅lima→−∞∫a1/(23)11+(6x)2dx=6⋅lima→−∞[16arctan⁡(6x)]a1/(23)=lima→−∞[arctan⁡(3)−arctan⁡(6a)]=π3−lima→−∞[arctan⁡(6a)]. Now, recall the end behavior of the function y=arctan⁡(6x), shown in the graph below:
